title: Dublin anti-lockdown public assembly
location: Dublin city centre: initial assembly in the Grafton Street area; BreakingNews reports protesters later walked to the GPO on O’Connell Street. It also reports earlier closure of St Stephen’s Green and Iveagh Gardens.
organizer: Unknown; neither read report names an organizer.
participants_original: BreakingNews reports “hundreds” gathered; no exact estimate or named estimator.
threshold_50_evidence: BreakingNews reports hundreds gathered to protest current Covid-19 restrictions, supporting the public-assembly threshold of at least 50. Do not infer a precise bound.

title.summary: Garda describes a later protest during the 27 February gathering; BreakingNews identifies it as an anti-lockdown demonstration.

start_date.summary: Both sources date the event to 27 February 2021. Garda says people began assembling around 1:30 p.m.; BreakingNews says a protest was due at 2 p.m. No exact first-arrival time is established.

end_date.summary: Neither read report establishes when the assembly physically ended. Garda says calm returned after intervention, which is not an exact end time.

location.summary: Garda places initial assembly in the Grafton Street area; BreakingNews reports movement to the GPO on O’Connell Street and prior closures of St Stephen’s Green and Iveagh Gardens.

scope.summary: The report describes one local Dublin city-centre event; it does not document a coordinated action elsewhere.

organizer.summary: Neither article identifies a protest organizer.

demands.summary: BreakingNews says people gathered to protest current Covid-19 restrictions. This supports the broad social_restrictions category; no particular measure or detailed platform is reported.

participants_original.summary: BreakingNews uses the qualitative description “hundreds”; no exact headcount or named estimating source is provided.

participants_min.summary: The qualitative report of hundreds supports the >=50 threshold but does not provide an exact numeric lower bound for coding.

participants_max.summary: No numerical upper bound is reported.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: BreakingNews reports hundreds gathered at the protest. This is clear qualitative evidence above 50; no exact count is assigned.

protester_violence.summary: Both reports describe some protesters throwing fireworks/firecrackers; Garda additionally reports missiles and spit directed at Garda members. This supports yes for reported acts, not a claim about every attendee.

accommodation.summary: No meeting, negotiation or agreement to a demand is reported; the policing plan and park closures do not establish accommodation.

arrests.summary: Garda reports 23 arrests; BreakingNews also reports arrests, but editorial or reporting independence from the official account is unestablished.

beatings.summary: No read report states that Gardaí beat protesters. Injuries to Garda personnel do not establish beatings of protesters.

crowd_dispersal.summary: Garda reports intervention and a return to calm, but neither source establishes an attempt to move and break up the crowd as a distinct dispersal action.

ignore.summary: The sources report a policing plan and arrests but do not establish whether the Irish state ignored the protest demand.

killings.summary: Neither read report establishes a state killing of a protester; silence is not coded as no.

shootings.summary: Neither read report establishes a state shooting at this event; silence is not coded as no.

notes: The event is dated 27 February by both read sources. Garda reports assembly from about 1:30 p.m.; BreakingNews says a protest was due at 2 p.m. and reports hundreds, current Covid-19 restrictions, a route to the GPO, fireworks and arrests. The demand is broadly state-directed but no detailed platform or organizer is named. Garda reports 23 arrests and three injured Garda personnel; these are not turnout counts or protester casualties. The 17 March Herbert Park search lead (S012) is outside February and has no established link to this event. No official MM ID or merge is assigned.
open_questions: Can an independent contemporaneous source give an attendance estimate and identify its basis?
Who organized the gathering, and which specific restrictions or policies did participants demand be changed?
When did the assembly physically end, and was any attempted crowd dispersal reported?
Are any related February or March Dublin actions part of the same organized episode, or separate local events?
Do additional sources corroborate the official arrest and violence account and identify further state responses?
